title: Radio Flashes and Torn Stars
description: A fast radio burst lasts a thousandth of a second and comes from another galaxy. On its way it crosses free electrons, which slow the low frequencies more than the high, so it arrives as a sweep: how long a sweep says how much gas it crossed, and so the bursts have weighed the gas between galaxies that nothing else could see. Some come from magnetars. A star that strays too near a supermassive black hole is torn into a stream and half of it falls in, flaring for months: a tidal disruption event. Adds both to the Radio Telescope and the Burst Observatory.

puzzle.goal: A pulse crossing a dispersion measure DM (in pc/cm³) arrives later at lower frequency. Write the delay Δt in ms between frequencies f₁ < f₂ (in GHz), with the constant 4.15 ms.
puzzle.name: Dispersion delay
puzzle.ask: Find Δt in ms for DM = @{DM}, f₁ = 1.2 GHz and f₂ = 1.5 GHz.
puzzle.method: In a plasma the group speed falls short of c by an amount growing as the plasma frequency squared over f²: integrate over the path.
